name: Civil unrest
value: France protests ebb; no deadly unrest
summary: French living-cost protests drew 106,000 on 14 Nov, the lowest turnout since 17 Oct; no deadly unrest found
state: French authorities counted 106,000 protesters on 14 Nov, including 24,000 in Paris, the lowest turnout since the movement began on 17 Oct, down from 550,000 that day; incidents were reported in Nantes, Lyon and Paris and no deaths (ARA, 14 Nov). Police used tear gas in several cities (Malay Mail/AFP, 15 Nov). Significant protests keep Watch; searches on 23 Nov found no deadly nationwide unrest or major crackdown in a large country.
for_you: Protests in France can disrupt transport in city centres at weekends. Travellers should follow FCDO travel advice and local authority guidance.
rubric_hit: Significant protests in France = Watch; no deadly nationwide unrest

sources.title: ARA — Protests in France continue but record lower participation
Malay Mail (AFP) — More than 100,000 march across France as protests enter fifth weekend

why: Mass protest and state crackdowns signal political fragility and can topple governments.
drivers: Cost of living, elections, corruption, repression, food and fuel prices.

rubric.alert: Deadly nationwide unrest or a state crackdown in a major country.
rubric.watch: Significant protests in several countries or deadly unrest in one.
rubric.normal: No deadly mass unrest in large countries.
